rules.what_is_seen: The lower roofs drawn around the third-floor block form one long east-west bar, the main roof about four times longer than it is deep and extended further by the offset north-east wing roof, although height cannot be read in plan.

Two parallel east-west hipped roof bars are drawn, a long southern main bar and a northern bar set back and offset toward the east that overlap only at the central block holding the stair, so the footprint reads as a stepped elongated shape, and on this floor the dressing room, bath and closets are gathered in a narrow strip on the east side between the bedrooms.

The third-floor block is organised around the central stair (marked UP from below) with a hatched masonry chimney mass containing a flue void standing beside the stair hall between the north-west bedroom and the master bedroom at mid-length of the main roof, the hall passing it on the east; no hearth opening is drawn at this level.

The ends of the main bar appear here only as hipped roof planes over the lower storeys, so no prow bay can be seen; the third-floor bedrooms are plain rectangles whose end walls are full-width casement groups between small piers.

Every roof plane drawn is hipped, with hip lines converging on east-west ridges at both ends of the main roof and at the end of the north-east wing roof, and the roof edges are drawn as thin double fascia lines; pitch and overhang depth are not readable in plan.

The small third-floor block sits set back from every roof edge near the middle of the long roof plan, over the stair and chimney mass, while the roofs step down to the east and west ends and to the offset north-east wing, so the plan massing is asymmetrical overall.

On every exterior wall of the third-floor bedrooms casement lights alternate with short square piers in continuous bands (the west wall of one bedroom, the east wall of the other, the full south wall of the master bedroom and the north wall between hatched piers) on a regular pier-to-pier module of roughly four feet by the scale bar, no dimensions being given.
In plan the masonry appears only as diagonal section hatching and wall tops as plain outlines, so brick coursing and cap bands cannot be read.
No glazing pattern is drawn at this 1/8-inch plan scale; windows are shown only as piers, frame lines and swing arcs.

Beyond the roof edges thin-line low walls run out from the building to plain square piers at their ends and corners at the south-west, south-east and north-west, with nested wall outlines at the west end; copings and planter profiles are not readable in plan.

The living and dining rooms and their south wall are not drawn at this level; the master bedroom's long south wall is a continuous band of casements between piers, but no balcony or glazed doors can be identified.

The third floor has no exterior door at all and is reached only by the internal stair marked UP from the floor below; every outer-wall opening is a casement between piers and no steps, path, porch or canopy are drawn.
The chimney appears only as a hatched masonry mass with a rectangular flue void in plan, so its height, cap and slot openings cannot be seen.
At 1/8-inch plan scale no trim, cap, foot or furniture profiles are drawn.

Every bay between piers on the third-floor exterior walls is drawn with a casement swing arc and no framed solid infill panel is identifiable, but panel texture cannot be read in plan and the rule is only a sometimes rule.

do_not_list.what_is_seen: The third floor has no exterior door, steps, path or canopy; it is reached only by the internal stair marked UP, and every outer-wall opening is a casement between piers.

The plan massing is asymmetrical: the third-floor block sits off-centre on the long main roof, the north-east wing roof is offset to the east, and the block itself steps unequally with the master bedroom projecting south and the dressing room and closets on the east side only.
At 1/8-inch plan scale no mouldings, mantels or ornament are drawn.
Masonry is shown only as diagonal section hatching in plan; no brick face or joints are drawn.
Every roof drawn is hipped at both ends, with hip lines converging on the ridges and no gable ends anywhere in the roof plan; pitch cannot be read in plan.
No hearth is drawn at this level; the hatched chimney mass with its flue void stands at the centre of the block beside the stair hall between the bedrooms, but the fireplace itself is not shown.

notes: Sheet 4 of 14, Third Floor Plan at 1/8 inch to 1 foot with no dimensions: a compact belvedere block of three bedrooms (two labelled BEDROOM, one MASTER BEDROOM), a dressing room with an inserted doorway noted, closets and a central stair, drawn together with the hipped roofs of the lower storeys and the thin-line garden walls and piers around it. Elevation, section and detail rules (brick coursing, cap bands, leaded glass, chimney slots, stepped profiles, stippled panels) cannot be read from this plan, so they are marked not_assessable rather than inferred.
